sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Sales of Musical Instruments and Studio Audio Gear

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental Napoleonic tradition; commercial companies governed by the amended Law of 10 August 1915)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU Single Market framework (freedom of establishment and free movement of goods and services)

Convention between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (1996, as amended by protocols)
Agreement between the Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union and the People's Republic of China on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (1984, with 2005 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, as amended; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs; Règlement grand-ducal du 23 février 2019 relatif à la mise en œuvre du Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Fully_Public with statutory data-tiering: public access is granted to UBO identity and extent of beneficial interest; residential address and certain personal data fields are restricted to obliged entities and competent authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document of each shareholder, manager and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/identity authority of the document holder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing state is party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization by the Luxembourg embassy/consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, articles of association and certificate of good standing of any corporate shareholder or parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry of the corporate shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-HCCH issuing states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire / police clearance certificate) for each proposed manager and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or competent judicial authority of the manager's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-HCCH issuing states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each shareholder and UBO (official utility bill, municipal resident certificate, or bank statement, not older than three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal registry, utility provider or regulated credit institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-HCCH issuing states; notarized translation into French/German if required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, managers and UBOs against EU and UN consolidated sanctions lists, the Luxembourg national freezing list, the U.S. OFAC SDN list, and PEP databases; enhanced due diligence applies if any PEP, sanction hit, or adverse media is identified; for a low-risk retail e-commerce entity, standard CDD is maintained but cannot be waived.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), official portal www.lbr.lu; name reservation is filed by a Luxembourg notary through the RCS online reservation module.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin characters; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated/romanized. The legal form marker 'S.à r.l.' or 'SARL' must be appended. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names, must not be misleading, contrary to public order or good morals, and must not imply a legal form other than the actual one.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque/Bank: requires prior authorization from the CSSF
Assurance/Réassurance: requires prior authorization from the Commissariat aux Assurances
Bourse/Stock exchange: requires prior regulatory approval
Crédit: requires prior authorization from the CSSF
Trust/Fiduciaire: requires prior regulatory or ministerial approval
Fonds d'investissement/OPCVM/SICAV/Société d'investissement: requires prior CSSF authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations may be renewed once for an additional 90 days upon application by the notary before expiry. If the LBR/RCS rejects a name on grounds of non-availability, confusion, misleading character or unlawfulness, the applicant may either file a new name reservation or bring a recours en réformation before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within one month of notification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a licensed domiciliation agent regulated under the Law of 31 May 1999; the registered office must be a physical address in Luxembourg with a local representative and mail-handling facility. A bare PO Box or non-physical virtual drop is not sufficient for an SARL.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated annual probability of unannounced physical inspection for a non-regulated online retail company is approximately 5%, though the RCS, tax and AML authorities may conduct ad hoc checks of registered-office substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional legal advisory, AML/UBO due-diligence file preparation and corporate structuring review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm / professional service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a simple single-member SARL incorporation file

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and issuance of non-confusion certificate (certificat de non-confusion)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCS/LBR fee schedule for online name reservation plus notary handling fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of articles of association and incorporation deed (acte constitutif)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff under Luxembourg notarial fee legislation; market benchmark for a standard SARL deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration fee at the RCS (immatriculation de la société)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS registration scale calculated on share capital; approximate minimum for SARL

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation excerpt in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
Registration of beneficial owners with the RBE declaration (filed by notary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: RBE statutory fee is zero; notary handling charge covers verification and electronic filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translations of foreign corporate documents into French/German plus apostille/consular legalization fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator and foreign competent authorities / Luxembourg consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille/legalization fees per issuing state and prevailing court-interpreter translation tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation service (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a non-regulated commercial company domiciliation contract

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended, SARL provisions under Title V (Articles 179 to 210); Grand-Ducal Regulations on the RCS and electronic publication.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg; electronic filing via lbr.lu and guichet.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif de société) containing the Articles of Association (Statuts), accompanied by the RCS incorporation application form (Form C1).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: €12,000 minimum share capital for a standard SARL; cash subscriptions must be at least 25% paid up at incorporation (€3,000 minimum), fully subscribed in the articles; all cash subscriptions must be deposited into a blocked escrow account in the name of the société en formation and released only upon RCS registration; any unpaid balance must be payable on demand of the management.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: INITIAL RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER AND FIRST BOARD OF MANAGERS. RESOLVED: 1. The initial board approves the subscription of the full issued share capital of €12,000 divided into 1,000 equal shares and confirms receipt of the statutory minimum paid-up capital of €3,000 held in the company's blocked escrow account. 2. The registered office of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée is fixed at [registered office in Luxembourg]. 3. [Full name] is appointed as the managing officer (gérant) with exclusive representation powers and as responsible for all filings with Luxembourg Business Registers. 4. All incorporation expenses and preliminaries are ratified and adopted. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Approval of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) in cooperation with the shareholders' advisors; no government filing yet.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to draft the acte constitutif and statuts. Verify the company name availability through the RCS/LBR online name search. The articles must include the SARL legal form, share capital, corporate object limited to online sale of musical instruments and studio audio equipment (ISIC 4791), registered office, duration, manager appointment and fiscal year. Obtain the authorised signature of the shareholders and record the subscription list.
required_dossiers: Draft notarial deed of incorporation and articles of association
Certificate of capital deposit or bank blocking confirmation
Subscription list signed by each shareholder
Identity document or passport of each shareholder and manager
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or authorization)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a deficiency such as missing identity documents, insufficient object precision or a name conflict, correct the draft immediately and reschedule the notarial appointment; amend the articles by separate notarial instrument if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Escrow Account and Deposit of Minimum Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the 'société en formation' at a Luxembourg bank approved by the notary. Deposit at least €3,000 of the capital in cash; obtain a bank certificate confirming the deposit and blocking of funds until the RCS registration is completed. The certificate must state the account holder name, amount, date and availability condition.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application
Draft articles of association and notarial mandate
Identity documents of shareholders and managers
Signed subscription list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional KYC clarification or business plan details, furnish the requested source-of-funds evidence and business plan promptly; if the bank unreasonably delays, apply to another Luxembourg licensed credit institution and inform the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend the notarial appointment with all shareholders and the appointed manager. The notary reads the deed, verifies the bank capitalization certificate, confirms the minimum paid-up capital requirement and executes the act. The manager signs an acceptance declaration. The notary also arranges the immediate electronic transmission to the RCS if applicable.
required_dossiers: Original bank certificate of capital deposit
Final draft notarial deed approved by shareholders
Passport or national ID of all signatories
Manager's signed acceptance of appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a shareholder or manager fails to appear, a proxy may be granted by notarial power of attorney in accordance with Luxembourg law; the notary may also appoint a sub-notary to execute the signing ceremony on a new date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Registration with Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or authorised professional files the incorporation package electronically with the RCS, pays the €32 registration fee, and requests publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RES). The RCS performs a legality and completeness check and issues the RCS registration number and certificate of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Executed notarial deed of incorporation
RCS incorporation application form (Form C1)
Confirmation of registration fee payment
Bank capital certificate
Identity and address details of all managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues an objection or requests clarifications, submit a memorandum with the corrected pages and supporting exhibits within the prescribed deadline; if the refusal is unjustified, lodge an appeal with the Luxembourg district court within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Official Publication and Obtaining the RCS Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS electronic publication (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the RCS has published the deed and registration. Request a certified extract of the RCS registration (extrait du registre de commerce), which formally evidences the company's legal personality and registration number. Keep the extract for subsequent tax and operational filings.
required_dossiers: No additional dossier - extract is issued upon request after registration publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication notice is delayed, verify the payment status of the publication fee, contact the RCS support service with the file reference, and request a confirmation of publication date; if needed, obtain a provisional certificate from the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social Security and Establishment Permit Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Ministry of the Economy via Guichet.lu; local municipal authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after incorporation: register the company for corporate income tax, VAT and obtain a VAT identification number via Guichet.lu; affiliate the company and its managers for social security at the CCSS; apply for the autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) with the Ministry of the Economy; verify municipal zoning compliance for any office, warehouse or showroom.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Registered office lease agreement or ownership deed
Fiscal domicile declaration
Identity documents and criminal records excerpts for managers
Company business plan where required by the competent authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment permit application is queried, submit supplementary documentation and reply to the notice within 15 days; if the permit is refused, lodge a motivated appeal with the Minister of the Economy and, if necessary, an appeal to the Luxembourg Administrative Court within one month.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie), Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes, via Guichet.lu; local municipal authority (Commune) for premises-related permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) - commercial class F1; additionally, a municipal operating licence/occupancy permit may be required for any physical storage, warehouse or retail area.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement / Department of Environment, Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development (Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et du Développement durable).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity of online retailing of musical instruments and studio audio equipment is not listed in Annex I of the Grand-Ducal Regulation implementing the Environmental Impact Assessment Directive; no full EIA or environmental operating permit is required provided there is no manufacturing, coating, or storage exceeding regulatory thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission thresholds apply to a pure retail and storage operation; any sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer regulations; packaging waste must be sorted and recorded under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste and the EU Waste Framework Directive (2008/98/EC).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (attestation incendie) issued by the competent fire brigade for any building open to the public or used as storage; compliance with ITM (Inspection du Travail et des Mines) workplace safety rules; structural load inspection by a licensed engineer if heavy audio equipment racks are installed; an employer's occupational health risk assessment (POEL) must be completed for all employees and the workplace should maintain a registre de sécurité as required by law.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — direct corporate income tax and national tax number; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — VAT registration and administration. Primary portals: myGuichet.lu / MyTVA; official information portals: impotsdirects.public.lu and aedt.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SARL, incorporation with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) produces an RCS registration number, and the ACD allocates a direct-tax identification number (matricule fiscale). For VAT, the entity must file a separate Luxembourg VAT registration application with the AEDT through myGuichet.lu, attaching the RCS extract, articles of association, proof of Luxembourg business address, identification of managers, and a description of intended taxable activities. A foreign non-EU entity without Luxembourg establishment must appoint an AEDT-approved Luxembourg tax representative; an EU-established taxable person may register directly. The AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number bearing the 'LU' prefix, which must be obtained before invoicing for taxable Luxembourg supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the resident SARL is treated as a separate Luxembourg corporate tax subject; it is taxable at entity level on worldwide income, with treaty-based and statutory territorial exemptions for eligible foreign permanent establishments and qualifying participation income under the Luxembourg participation exemption regime; no pass-through or check-the-box treatment is available).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box election regime. The principal statutory elections are: (1) fiscal unity ('intégration fiscale') for corporate income tax and municipal business tax grouping among Luxembourg-resident companies satisfying the 95% capital/control thresholds; (2) VAT grouping ('assujetti unique') election for closely linked taxable persons; and (3) participation exemption election for qualifying EU and non-EU shareholdings subject to conditions. Hybrid mismatch reclassification elections are prohibited or constrained by ATAD transposition and Luxembourg domestic anti-hybrid rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (Luxembourg small-enterprise exemption threshold on annual taxable turnover excluding VAT; registration is mandatory when turnover exceeds this ceiling. For intra-EU distance sales to consumers, the EU-wide OSS threshold is EUR 10,000, above which VAT must be accounted for in the destination Member State through the OSS scheme, independent of Luxembourg domestic turnover).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently has no general real-time fiscal clearance regime, continuous transaction control API obligation, or mandatory digital stamping for standard B2B VAT invoices. Luxembourg has announced a phased transition towards EU-compliant B2B e-invoicing and electronic reporting, expected to become mandatory in alignment with EU legislative efforts (ViDA/SIMPL) likely from or after 2026. Until such mandate is in force, VAT returns and recapitulative statements must be filed electronically through MyTVA, SAF-T-compatible records must be maintained for tax audit purposes, and cross-border payment data must be reported to CESOP by payment service providers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Sales of musical instruments and studio audio gear qualify for 0% VAT when the goods are supplied to a non-EU destination and the SARL, a customer, or a third party acting on the SARL's behalf removes the goods physically outside the European Union within the statutory export period. Eligible ancillary services (e.g., transport handling, loading, freight, and intermediary services directly linked to the export) may also be zero-rated. Intra-EU distance sales to final consumers do not qualify for export zero-rating; they are taxable in the destination Member State under OSS/IOSS. The SARL must retain full customs and transport evidence proving physical export before applying the 0% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (EX/A) accepted by Luxembourg customs authorities
Bill of lading / airway bill / CMR consignment note
Inward remittance certificate or bank/payment evidence showing receipt of consideration from the foreign buyer
Customs clearance and transport documentation demonstrating physical removal from the EU
Export ledger / VAT export register reconciling each invoice to the corresponding customs declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg Customs scrutinize export zero-rating claims strictly. If export or proof-of-receipt conditions are not substantiated, AEDT may reassess VAT at 17%, impose late-payment interest and administrative fines, and claw back any input VAT recovered in respect of the export. In cases of fraudulent zero-rating or wilful misrepresentation, criminal proceedings may result in significant fines and imprisonment, and retroactive tax reassessments may extend to the full limitation period. All export documentation, payment evidence, and FX repatriation records must be retained for at least six years, or longer if an investigation or litigation is pending.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank (ECB). Prudential supervision and licensing of credit institutions and e-money institutions in Luxembourg are exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the Luxembourg Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector, as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Luxembourg for both current and capital account transactions. The TFEU free movement of capital (Article 63) and the Law of 5 April 1993 impose no exchange controls, no prior licensing, and no mandatory conversion for trade settlements, dividend remittances, loan repayments, or capital injections. Profit remittance from a Luxembourg SARL is treated as a dividend subject to 15% Luxembourg withholding tax, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) when the corporate beneficiary holds, for an uninterrupted 12-month period, at least 10% of the capital, or reduced under applicable double-tax treaties (commonly 5–15%). The only tax-law hurdle is the balance-sheet test for distributions: the SARL may distribute only if net assets exceed the statutory capital plus non-distributable reserves. The only administrative friction is the paying bank's KYC documentation and the BCL's balance-of-payments statistical reporting for direct investment and treasury flows; these are declarative, not consent-based controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable — Luxembourg maintains full freedom of payment and no surrender rule. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation of export sales proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio (0% compulsory conversion; 100% may be freely retained). Receivables from the online sale of musical instruments and studio audio gear may be held in EUR, USD, CNY, GBP, or any convertible currency in Luxembourg or foreign accounts, provided that intra-group arrangements respect the arm's-length transfer-pricing standard, monetary items are translated at closing rates for statutory accounts (unrealised FX gains/losses are recognised in the profit and loss account), and cross-border flows are declared to the BCL for statistical purposes where thresholds apply. No exporter FX card and no Central Bank approval is required for retention or conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) and multi-currency Operational Account (EUR/USD/GBP)
Operational Account (EUR and multi-currency) with treasury pooling; capital escrow available
Operational and Settlement Accounts (EUR, USD); commercial trade services; escrow deposits
Operational Account (EUR) oriented to corporate and private clients
Operational current account (EUR) for transactional banking

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Overall feasibility rating: High as an ancillary collection/payment rail; Low-Medium as the sole primary banking layer. PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. et Cie S.C.A. is a Luxembourg-regulated credit institution under CSSF supervision and is therefore fully acceptable for the SARL's merchant settlement. Stripe is established as an Irish EMI passporting into the EEA under the E-Money Directive and PSD2, and is lawful where the settlement liquidity is swept into the SARL's own bank account. Non-EEA EMIs (notably UK-licensed entities post-Brexit) may not passport and require a Luxembourg branch or a new EU-licensed subsidiary. Legal constraints include EMI safeguarding and client-asset segregation, prohibition of lending and investment services, CSSF notification/registration for payment services provided in Luxembourg, and the absence of overdraft or credit facilities; the SARL's statutory capital escrow and primary treasury must therefore remain with a full credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De facto market mandate: at least one physical KYC interview is required by the major banks (BGL BNP Paribas, BIL, SGBT, Banque de Luxembourg) for non-resident directors/UBOs and for all newly incorporated SARLs without a pre-existing banking record. Remote/video onboarding is possible only for low-risk EU-resident clients with fully digitalised documentation, consistent with the CSSF AML/CFT framework (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended); in practice, the gérant and UBO should travel to Luxembourg (or a designated foreign representative office) for a one-to-two-day compliance meeting, signature of account documents, and activation of e-banking tokens. No-travel onboarding typically extends the opening timeline from two-to-three weeks to six-to-ten weeks and materially raises the risk of refusal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO with no EU tax residency or thin economic substance in Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled passport copies of all UBOs and directors; tax residency certificates from the home tax authority; sworn declaration of source of wealth and source of funds supported by bank statements, asset-sale agreements and salary records; complete corporate ownership chart identifying every intermediary; notarised board resolutions of the SARL; professional reference letter from the UBO's home bank; commitment to maintain Luxembourg substance (registered office, local gérant, VAT and CIT filings, annual general meeting).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket online retail flow through Stripe/PayPal without documentary trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Stripe and PayPal merchant agreements; at least six months of settlement/card statements or a detailed launch budget for a new SARL; website VAT and EU OSS/e-commerce registration proof; supplier purchase invoices for musical-instrument and audio inventory; logistics and customs declarations; cash-flow forecast consistent with ISIC 4791 e-commerce retail; documented transaction-monitoring controls and a commitment to reject third-party card funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital subscription funded from a third party's account or by a non-UBO lender
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised deed of incorporation (acte de constitution) stating the EUR 12,000 minimum subscribed capital (at least 25% paid up at incorporation); bank issue certificate from the receiving bank; share register and subscription receipts; funding-origin statement with remitter's KYC file; signed shareholder loan or gift agreement where funds are borrowed; sworn declaration that no third party exercises control or beneficial interest over the SARL shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment chains involving high-risk jurisdictions or freight-forwarding consignees
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: List of commercial counterparties with country-risk ratings; transport and Incoterms contracts for each jurisdiction; EU/OFAC/UN sanctions screening output for UBOs, customers and suppliers; customs entries and EUR1 or certificate-of-origin documentation where applicable; commitment to SWIFT purpose-code transparency and to reject any payment with incomplete reference; US state nexus registration and sales-tax permits where US distribution is material.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected treasury netting or cash-pooling flows between the SARL and an affiliated purchasing or IP company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed intercompany services and supply agreements; Luxembourg transfer-pricing documentation aligned with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and the Luxembourg transfer-pricing circular (LIR circular n° 56/1 R); annual TP report and benchmark study for e-commerce distribution functions; board-approved treasury policy describing FX hedging, liquidity buffers and zero-balance-account mechanics; advance pricing arrangement (APA) filing where intercompany volumes exceed EUR 1 million or cross-border inventory risk is material.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Standard compliant sequence: (1) the shareholder/gérant executes the notarial draft deed; (2) the bank opens a blocked account in the name of the future SARL; (3) the remitter transmits a SWIFT MT103 with reference 'Souscription au capital — SARL [name] — RCS [future registration no.]' and completes the bank's source-of-funds questionnaire; the remitter must be the UBO or an identifiable shareholder, never an anonymous third party; (4) the bank issues an attestation de blocage confirming receipt of the minimum subscribed capital of EUR 12,000 (statutorily at least 25% paid-up; market practice blocks the full amount); (5) the notary files the incorporation at the RCS Luxembourg; (6) after publication in the RESA, the block is lifted and the funds are swept into the operational EUR account. For shareholder loans, the wire reference must state 'Advance / shareholder loan — board approved' with a signed loan agreement and an arm's-length interest rate to prevent reclassification as hidden equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Treasury clearing rails by payment class: (i) EU/SEPA supplier invoices — SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT or SEPA Instant) in EUR with the invoice number and reverse-charge reference in the structured creditor identifier; (ii) non-EUR or third-country suppliers — SWIFT MT103 (single customer payment) or MT202 COV (cover payment) with purpose code 'Trade payment for musical instruments and audio gear', Incoterms and customs entry numbers; (iii) high-value or documentary-risk procurement (e.g., Asian OEM components) — irrevocable commercial Letter of Credit issued under UCP 600 with confirmation by a top-rated correspondent bank and an ICC-compliant document set (commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin); (iv) receivables settlement — Stripe and PayPal payout wires (SCT or SWIFT) are credited daily to the operational account and swept via zero-balance account (ZBA) into a treasury term deposit; (v) intra-group supplier clearing — Luxembourg cash pooling and netting with signed intercompany agreements and transfer-pricing documentation. All disbursement wires must carry a true and complete purpose statement; cash disbursements above EUR 10,000 are prohibited by EU AML/CFT rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (plain vanilla EUR/USD, EUR/CNH, EUR/GBP) with a CSSF-licensed credit institution under an ISDA Master Agreement and EMIR clearing or margin rules
Vanilla FX options (European calls and puts) and zero-cost collars/tunnels referenced to USD sales receipts from Stripe and PayPal settlement
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) to align USD-denominated marketplace income with EUR-denominated supplier, payroll and tax liabilities
Listed currency futures and options on EU-regulated venues (EUREX, Euronext) as exchange-cleared micro-hedges

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) strictly limited to offshore non-convertible or restricted currencies (CNH, INR, BRL) with OECD-licensed counterparties and a written board-approved hedging policy demonstrating underlying trade exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and statutory financial statements deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the close of the financial year; for a calendar-year SARL, on or before 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a formal reminder, then a coercive fine imposed by the District Court; continuing default may lead to criminal fines against officers and administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS registered corporate data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to respond to the annual confirmation invitation results in a formal notice, potential coercive fine ordered by the District Court, and, after repeated defaults, dissolution and strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE/Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or knowingly incorrect data triggers a reminder, publication on the RBE non-compliance list, and criminal sanctions (fines and/or imprisonment) under Luxembourg anti-money-laundering law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and net wealth tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a financial year ending 31 December, on or before 31 December of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger automatic official tax assessment, late-payment interest, a late-filing penalty of 10% per month of tax due, and potential distraint measures for sustained non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required if the SARL exceeds two of the following three criteria on the balance-sheet date: total balance sheet EUR 4,460,000; net turnover EUR 8,920,000; average annual employee headcount 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 10 June 2009 on annual accounts and consolidated accounts, as amended; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for consolidated financial statements and listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Any shareholding transfer must be reflected in the RBE within one month of the event. In addition, the SARL must complete the mandatory annual RBE confirmation between 1 and 31 January each year, confirming the identity of all beneficial owners on file.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% national CIT; plus 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax (aggregate 22.80% in Luxembourg City for CY2024)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income, effective tax rate approx. 4.56%), notional interest deduction (NID) on new equity, investment tax credit (up to 8% for qualifying tangible/rational investments), R&D incentives and business expansion measures

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modèle 1001 (Déclaration collective pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités et l'impôt commercial communal) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May of the calendar year following the fiscal year end; for a 31 December year-end, the statutory deadline is 31 May of the subsequent year (tax administration extensions may apply)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identity and contact: legal form, RCS Luxembourg number, registered office, tax file number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to a resident SARL; leave blank unless declaring a Luxembourg permanent establishment of a foreign company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the accounting period of the Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total commercial net profit before tax reclassifications (commercial balance sheet result).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State only profits attributable to the Luxembourg PE in accordance with the arm's length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for tax-deductible provisions, write-offs and depreciation (e.g., accounts receivable, inventory, fixed assets).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide PE-specific depreciation schedules and substantiation; general overhead allocations must be documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carryforward of prior-year tax losses used in the current assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses previously established for the same Luxembourg PE may be used; foreign losses are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after statutory allocation, loss offset and certain deductions (assiette imposable).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Final PE profit subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax and municipal business tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation: corporate income tax at 15%, solidarity surcharge at 7% on CIT, and municipal business tax at the communal rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Present separate tax computations for the PE; municipal business tax applies only if the PE is situated in a Luxembourg commune.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a formal reminder; subsequent failure exposes the company to an administrative fine of EUR 125, a default surcharge of up to 20% of the tax due, and monthly late-payment interest of 0.8% (compound). Intentional non-filing is classified as tax evasion and may lead to criminal sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A beneficial-owner shareholder residing in a treaty jurisdiction must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and present it, together with Luxembourg form 105 and proof of shareholding (10% or more for parent-subsidiary benefits), to the paying agent or Luxembourg tax administration in order to apply the reduced treaty rate at source or to claim a refund. Under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, a 0% withholding rate applies where the parent holds at least 10% for at least 12 uninterrupted months and satisfies anti-abuse substance conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: domestic law 0%; under most DTAs 0% or reduced rates of 5%–10%. Royalties: domestic law 0%; under most DTAs 0% for copyright royalties and 5%–10% for patent/industrial royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File: EUR 350,000,000 consolidated group revenue; Local File: cross-border controlled transactions exceeding EUR 100,000 per category of transactions (goods, services, IP).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies ATAD-aligned anti-abuse rules and the OECD BEPS Action 13 substance expectations. A SARL active in online retail (ISIC 4791) must demonstrate adequate business substance: physical premises, employees actively managing daily sales, bank accounts, books and records, board decision-making, and operational assets. Entities exploiting preferential regains such as the IP box must satisfy the nexus approach based on qualifying R&D expenditure. Failure to meet substance may result in treaty-shopping challenges, GAAR recharacterisation, and disregard of the legal entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a false Quotité de l'Impôt sur le Revenu des Collectivités (Modèle 1001), suppressing online sales revenue, booking fictitious costs, or colluding to shift taxable profits offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment up to five years; administrative penalties include a 20% surcharge on the evaded tax plus monthly 0.8% interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for taxes evaded when fraudulent conduct is proven; civil restitution of wrongly distributed amounts, travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment are possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to price cross-border transactions with related parties (inventory, e-commerce software licences, digital marketing services, royalties) on an arm's length basis and failing to prepare, update, and supply Local File/Master File documentation upon request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments increasing the Luxembourg taxable base; late-payment interest at 0.8% per month; a default penalty of up to 20% of the additional tax; and imposition of higher prevailing rates in the absence of compliant documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the SARL may be held civilly liable for the resulting underpayment if gross negligence is established; disqualification from management may follow in egregious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Disguising a dividend distribution to the sole foreign shareholder as management fees, royalties, or excessive interest payments, or distributing profits while deliberately omitting the 15% withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of disguised amounts as constructive dividends; levy of 15% withholding tax plus interest; 20% administrative surcharge; denial of deductible expenses for the hidden distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors become personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax; personal fines apply; repayments of improperly distributed monies may be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SARL as a brass-plate entity without real management and employees, using Luxembourg residency solely to access the DTA network while all substantive functions remain offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax residency may be challenged; the General Anti-Abuse Rule may recharacterise the structure, deny treaty protection, impose full Luxembourg taxation on global profits, and trigger penalties and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil piercing is available on proof of abuse of law; directors face civil restitution for distributions received with knowledge, travel bans in fraud proceedings, and personal criminal liability for tax sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of the annual Modèle 1001, failure to file ancillary returns (municipal business tax, withholding tax return), and refusal to provide transfer pricing documentation or accounting records after statutory request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 125 for the return; mandatory surcharge of up to 20% of the assessed tax; 0.8% monthly arrears interest; inability to claim loss carryforwards or treaty credits until compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be made personally liable for the fines and interest if the omission is intentional; repeated violations result in criminal liability and possible imprisonment.
